entities.summary: Giovanni Cristoforo Romano (1456–1512) was a renowned Italian Renaissance sculptor and medallist. He was born in a small town in Tuscany and began his artistic training at a young age. Romano's masterpieces, including the famous 'Pietà' sculpture, showcase his exceptional skill and attention to detail. His work had a profound impact on the development of Renaissance art, influencing generations of artists to come. The 'Pietà' is considered one of the greatest works of the Renaissance, and Romano's innovative techniques and use of marble helped to establish him as one of the leading artists of his time. Despite his relatively short career, Romano left a lasting legacy in the world of art. His contributions to the artistic movement paved the way for future innovators and continue to inspire artists today.
